content.title: Compounding Errors
content.content:
Compounding Errors
Agents loop on tool results. Even with 95% success per step, the chance of 20 consecutive successes is about 36%.
Source: Calculation simplified, assuming independent steps. METR “Time Horizon 1.1” (January 2026; Claude Opus 4.6 value after the March calculation fix). Same as Lecture 1, page 9.
36% at 20 steps
Task length AI can handle (METR)
Doubles about every 4 months

About 12 hours

content.title: Why measurable goals matter
content.content:
Why measurable goals matter
Errors pile up when intermediate results go unchecked. With a condition you can measure every time, you can get back on track.
Source: Docs and announcements for OpenAI Codex CLI (/goal, v0.128.0, April 2026) and Claude Code (/goal, v2.1.139, May 2026).
Write done-conditions as numbers or true/false
Not measurable
Measurable
“Fix it nicely”
All tests pass, and lint passes
“Make it faster”
Benchmark score of 90 or higher
“Reduce bugs”
Zero type errors
Measurement lets you catch bad results on the spot and “go back”
Checking every iteration stops failures before they pile up. The next topic, autoresearch, builds on this idea.
Example: goal mode (/goal)
/goal <done-condition>
Keeps going until the condition is met
Write the condition once; no need to repeat the instruction. Codex and Claude Code added this feature in spring 2026.
A separate model judges
In Claude Code, a small, fast model (Haiku by default) checks the condition after every turn.

content.title: Human in the loop
content.content:
Human in the loop
For irreversible operations such as sending email or deleting files, have a human confirm before execution.
Source: Claude Code Docs “Settings”, “Permission modes”, “Configure auto mode” (checked 2026/10). Approval screen recreated from Claude Code's display.
Claude Code approval screen
Bash(git push origin main)
  Push local commits to remote
Do you want to proceed?
> 1. Yes
  2. Yes, and don't ask again for git push
  3. No, and tell Claude what to do differently
(In Claude Code) Settings decide how much to ask
Ask every time (default mode)
Asks a human for each new type of operation.
Set rules in advance (settings.json)
allow = run without asking, ask = always ask, deny = forbidden.
deny applies in every mode.
Let another model decide (auto mode).
A classifier (another model) checks each time instead of a human.
Blocks only irreversible or unrequested actions.
Never ask (bypassPermissions)
Runs everything without confirmation.

content.title: Human in the loop
content.content:
Human in the loop
Choosing human-in, on or out-of-the-loop changes how you build approval and stopping mechanisms.
There is a trade-off between convenience and security.
Source: The categories come from the autonomous weapons debate in Human Rights Watch “Losing Humanity” (2012/11/19). Anthropic “Measuring AI agent autonomy in practice” (2026/2/18), Anthropic “How we contain Claude across products” (2026/5/25).
in: approve every time
Agent
Action
Approval for every action
A human allows every operation.
Approval often becomes a mere formality.
on: watch, able to stop
Agent
Action
Watch & stop
Agent runs on its own; a human monitors and intervenes if needed.
Assumes the stop mechanism is outside the agent.
out: fully delegated
Agent
Action
See results only
Humans see only the results. Scheduled or unattended runs.
Stopping and reporting must be built into the system.

content.title: Non-idempotent tools
content.content:
Non-idempotent tools
Case: The send succeeded, but the connection dropped before the response arrived; the agent judged it a failure and retried
Source: Based on Stripe API Reference “Idempotent requests” (checked 2026/10/24; explains that resending after a connection error may perform the same operation twice). The email scenario is a fictional example.
Agent
Email service
Recipient's inbox
① send_email (quote)
1st email arrives
×
Success response lost (timeout)
② Judged as failed
③ send_email again
2nd email arrives
Tools with similar risks
Place order
→ Ordered twice
Send money
→ Paid twice
Post
→ Duplicate posts
The agent can't tell success from failure. Even if the connection drops, the action may have executed on the other side.

content.title: Subagents
content.content:
Subagents
A subagent is another agent called by an agent. It separates context and saves the parent agent's context.
Source: Anthropic Claude Code Docs “Create custom subagents”, OpenAI Codex Docs “Subagents” (both checked 2026/10/27). Call counts and examples are illustrative.
When a parent agent investigates
Parent agent's context (accumulates from the top)
Request: fix the parse_date bug
Investigation log
search results ×6
File contents from read_file ×14
run_tests logs
The context fills up with investigation logs before the fix.
When delegating to a subagent
Parent agent's context (accumulates from the top)
Request: fix the parse_date bug
Agent("Find callers of parse_date")
Subagent investigates in its own context
search ×6, read_file ×14 (not in the main context)
Report: 3 callers; UTC conversion missing
Only the summary report enters the parent's context
Mix models: Stronger models (e.g., Opus) are assigned to harder decisions, while cheaper models (e.g., Haiku) are used for research.
Cuts costs: Claude Code lets you set a model for each subagent.

Passes tests on unsolvable tasks and reports failure as “complete.” Even judge models fail to catch the error.

content.content:

Those are all real incidents. In each case, the agent touched files that the task did not require.
